Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the all-important chase! Pakistan Women spread out to take the field followed by the two umpires who head to their positions. It will be Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma to open the innings for India Women. Sadia Iqbal is handed the new ball and will start the proceedings. Here we go..
... THE RUN CHASE ...

With the wicket offering very little assistance to the bowlers, this chase should be manageable for the in-form India Women batters. However, as the saying goes, 'It's never over until it's over!' India will still need to bat well, especially against the quality spinners in the Pakistan lineup, who will be eager to turn this into a competitive game. An exciting second essay is set to unfold! Stick around.

Choosing to bat first, Pakistan Women struggled to find confidence throughout their innings. Despite a promising start from Sidra Ameen, her soft dismissal marked the beginning of a steady fall of wickets. No batter showed the intent to settle in, instead opting for glory shots that were unnecessary given the situation. Tuba Hassan played a good hand, scoring 22, but was dismissed too. The only bright spot for Pakistan was a late cameo by Fatima Sana, which added some crucial runs, giving them a modest total to defend at the end of their innings.

Renuka Singh is in for a chat. She says that she is happy with the way she bowled in her return game. Shares that she was at the NCA before the tournament and the coaches there helped her a lot. Tells that there was help off the surface and the breeze was helping as well. Adds that her aim was to make the ball move as much as she could. Backs her batters to get the runs.

India Women have delivered an exceptional bowling performance to wrap Pakistan Women up for just 108 runs. After being asked to bowl first, Renuka Singh and Pooja Vastrakar set the tone early, with Pooja dismissing both openers within the first four overs. With Pakistan on the back foot, India Women introduced spin from both ends, making it difficult for the batters to rotate the strike. Forced into risky big shots, Pakistan lost a few more wickets. Renuka Singh returned for her final over, taking two wickets on consecutive deliveries, firmly placing India in control. The spinners specifically Deepti Sharma then closed out the innings with tight bowling chipping two wickets in an over which was complemented by another run-out to make it three in an over for India Women, limiting Pakistan to a below-par total that India will feel confident chasing on any day.

The ball goes through the gap between the bat and pad to rattle into the leg pole. Pakistan Women have been bowled out for 108!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for this blockbuster clash to commence. Harmanpreet Kaur leads her troops out to the middle followed by the two openers of Pakistan. It will be Gull Feroza and Muneeba Ali to open the innings for Pakistan. Renuka Singh has the new ball in hand and she is raring to go. A slip in place. Let's play...

PITCH REPORT - Isobel Joyce is near the deck. She starts by saying that there was good pace and bounce in the first game. Adds that the balls from spinners were holding up a bit. Opines that the wind has died down a bit since the latter half of the first game, but it will still be something the two teams will have to take into account. She expects India to use spin in the Powerplay as she feels that pacers will be slightly easier to hit.

The captain of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says that they are fine with doing both. Feels that the conditions will remain the same throughout the game. Tells that they have a chance to restrict Pakistan to a low total. States that every game is important for them and shares that getting into a rhythm from the first game will be crucial. Informs that they have made 3 changes from the last T20 they played against South Africa.

Nida Dar, the skipper of Pakistan Women says that the pitch looks dry and should favour batting. Adds that the team is well prepared to counter the wind at the venue which is similar to that in Karachi where they have practiced and played a lot of games. Talks about this being a great opportunity ahead of the World Cup. Further adds that they draw confidence from their win in the previous edition against India and they have a pretty balanced side to start well.
Pakistan Women (Playing XI) - Sidra Ameen, Gull Feroza, Muneeba Ali (WK), Aliya Riaz, Nida Dar (C), Iram Javed, Fatima Sana, Syeda Aroob Shah, Tuba Hassan, Sadia Iqbal, Nashra Sandhu.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Dayalan Hemalatha, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Jemimah Rodrigues, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Pooja Vastrakar, Radha Yadav, Shreyanka Patil, Renuka Singh.
TOSS - The coin goes up and it lands in the favour of Nida Dar. Pakistan Women have opted to BAT first.

In case you missed it, Nepal and UAE played the curtain-raiser earlier in the day, with Samjhana Khadka's 72 helping Nepal to their first-ever win in the history of the Women's Asia Cup. Nepal, returning to the competition after an eight-year gap, will next take on Pakistan while the UAE will face India.

On the flip side, Pakistan Women have faced a turbulent 18 months and will be desperate to make a strong start in the tournament. With a revamped lineup and strategic changes, they hope to find the winning formula. Nida Dar, at the helm, carries the weight of leading her team against formidable opponents. Will she inspire a turnaround for Pakistan Women as they challenge the dominant Women in Blue? Can Pakistan overcome their recent struggles and defy the odds? Or will India continue their reign, showcasing their supremacy once more? The stage is set, the anticipation is palpable, and the toss is just moments away. Stay tuned to witness this thrilling encounter unfold!

The spotlight shines brightly on Smriti Mandhana, who is hitting peak form, making India's batting lineup a force to be reckoned with. Additionally, Pooja Vastrakar and Deepti Sharma could prove to be crucial with the ball, adding to the team's strength and versatility as they aim to uphold their legacy in this tournament.

The opening day of the ACC Women's T20 Asia Cup 2024 couldn’t have been more thrilling, as two Group A powerhouses ignite the global anticipation that's been building. In match number 2, the India Women face off against the Pakistan Women at the renowned Rangiri Dambulla International Cricket Stadium in Dambulla. This high-stakes encounter is the perfect icing on the cake for a spectacular start to the tournament. These two teams have clashed six times in the Asia Cup, with India Women emerging as the dominant force, securing victories in five of those encounters while Pakistan Women have managed just one win so far. India Women enter this tournament riding high on the success of a multifaceted series against South Africa Women, where they tied the three-match T20I series at one-all, with one game being washed out. The Indian opening duo of Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana is in exceptional form, poised to be a formidable challenge for Pakistan Women, who will need to devise strategic plans to counter this top-order threat. Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur and Jemimah Rodrigues have been the sturdy pillars of the Indian batting lineup, proving to be a major part of the solid middle-order backbone. With the ball, much will depend on the expertise of Renuka Singh and Pooja Vastrakar to set the tone early on. Meanwhile, Deepti Sharma and Radha Yadav are expected to weave their magic with their spin, aiming to entangle the opposition in their web. This Indian side also boasts an impressive array of young talent who have already made their mark on the international stage, further cementing their status as a dominant force. This blend of youth and experience makes India Women an even more formidable and well-rounded team, fully prepared to defend their title. On the other side, Pakistan Women enter this tournament following a rather disappointing away series against England Women, where they lost all three T20I games. However, they will be looking to start this campaign on a high note against their arch-rivals, aiming to make a significant impact. Led by the formidable Nida Dar, who is expected to lead from the front, she will be a crucial player to watch throughout the tournament. Sidra Ameen and Muneeba Ali have been the consistent run-getters for the team, and Pakistan Women will once again rely on them to address their batting vulnerabilities, which have been a major concern in recent times. With the ball, much will depend on the skipper Nida Dar, supported by Sadia Iqbal and Fatima Sana, who will be looking to shine and deliver match-winning performances. With both these sides ready to battle it out and kickstart their campaigns on a winning note, the world eagerly awaits this edge-of-the-seat encounter. Who are you backing to win this one?
